clue.text: When speaking, which people produce bad luck?

indicators.note: When speaking says the phrase before it is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a question 'who do?' asks which people produce or perform

explanation.surface: A superstitious query about which folk bring misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'who do' and you hear the word for a jinx; the spelling is the one entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx or curse bringing misfortune is the sense, so it equals bad luck.

clue.text: Henry takes a few steps in the gloaming

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry
a flight is a short set of stairs

explanation.surface: A man named Henry walks up some stairs at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, when daylight is fading, is twilight, which is what gloaming means.

clue.text: A system of logic devised in Rangoon

indicators.note: devised in suggests the letters of the city are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A philosophical method was invented in Burma's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's logical works, and later Bacon's, were titled as an instrument of reasoning: a logical method.

clue.text: Long service is worth no consideration

definitions.meaning: a long serve in tennis lands beyond the lines of play
dismissed without a hearing, not worth considering

explanation.definitionFit: A serve landing past the lines is outside the playing area; a claim dismissed without trial is dismissed before a hearing.

clue.text: Linking judge with excessive suavity

parts.note: unction can mean an oily, excessively smooth manner

explanation.surface: A judge is described as joined to an overly smooth manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A joining point or connection is a link, so the noun matches the gerund 'Linking' used as a noun.

clue.text: Jack may be crazy

definitions.meaning: a jack is a ship's flag, and it may be hoisted on a mast
British slang for mad or deluded

explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a flag flown aloft; the phrase is also British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag hoisted aloft on a flagstaff, and slang meaning mad.

clue.text: Fish for tea

definitions.meaning: British slang for tea, as in a cup of the drink

explanation.definitionFit: A trout-like fish shares its name with British slang for tea, from Chinese.

clue.text: Vet in small, animal practice to start with

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside another

parts.note: an insect is a small creature

indicators.note: to start with asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon begins work at a small-animal clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small animal practice' reads as a vet's clinic, but 'small animal' is INSECT and P (from 'practice', 'to start with') goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it closely, the verb sense.

clue.text: Rover, faithful friend, got up

indicators.note: got up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Damon, of Damon and Pythias, is the classical model of a faithful friend

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover, loyal companion, got to its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like a dog's name; it means wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is a rover.

clue.text: Having entered innumerable races, taking first in each, he's bound to succeed

indicators.note: taking first in each asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A competitor who has won many races is sure of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The next in line to an inheritance or title is destined to follow.

clue.text: He's left something on a peg

parts.note: in cricket, the on side is also called the leg side
a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: Someone has hung an item on a hook.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket convention on = LEG (the leg side of the field) is the trick; 'left' means bequeathed, not abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A beneficiary of a will is someone to whom an item has been bequeathed.

clue.text: Initially they pay for restoration of a bar

indicators.note: Initially asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: a ransom is money paid to have a captive restored

explanation.surface: People seem to fund the refurbishment of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bar' reads like a pub being restored; it is the crosspiece over a door or window.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horizontal crosspiece of wood or stone, a beam above a door.

clue.text: Reorganised France's old army

indicators.note: Reorganised tells us to rearrange the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters of the word as written, possessive S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: France's former military has been restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground troops as a whole make up a nation's army, as opposed to its navy.

clue.text: Used to sound clue, for example

definitions.meaning: a weighted line dropped to measure the depth of water
a hint or pointer that guides a detective

explanation.definitionFit: The metal weight sailors use for depth-sounding shares its name with a detective's hint.

clue.text: T.V. personality's caress went .. wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A television presenter's affectionate touch was misjudged.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreader on television is a broadcasting personality.

clue.text: Travel north and see the city's sights by boat

parts.note: to go is to travel
to 'do' a city is to see its sights, and the city here is LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A tourist heads north and tours a city on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Sightseeing slang: tourists 'do LA' when they see its sights; the boat is the Venetian one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, flat-bottomed Venetian craft is a kind of boat.

clue.text: She was saved by a hero and a capital lawyer

definitions.text: She was saved by a hero

parts.note: taken as written
Rome is a capital city
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A woman is rescued by a champion and a big-city attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Perseus rescued her from a sea monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ethiopian princess of myth was chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Dance of extremely short duration

definitions.meaning: a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century
something lasting just a single stride, a moment

explanation.definitionFit: The ragtime ballroom dance shares its name with a single brief pace.

clue.text: A Quaker, by the sound of it; a Quaker who writes letters

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the name is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: William Penn was a famous Quaker who founded Pennsylvania
Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: A Quaker described as a member of the Society who corresponds.
explanation.walkthrough: PENN sounds like PEN; a Quaker is a FRIEND. The definition is 'one' who writes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent one has never met is someone who exchanges letters.

clue.text: Changing order in bureaucracy gradually diminished

indicators.note: Changing order in tells us the letters of a synonym are to be rearranged

parts.note: red tape is a nickname for bureaucracy

explanation.surface: Reshuffling the civil service slowly shrank something.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of RED TAPE, a synonym for bureaucracy, not of a word in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowed towards a point has dwindled bit by bit.

clue.text: Face pain showing confidence

parts.note: pan is slang for face
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone faces pain while appearing self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN is slang for the face, as in deadpan.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant self-assurance and style is the sense of flair.

clue.text: Old character's speech defect returns in time

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time

indicators.note: returns says the speech-defect word is read backwards

parts.note: a lisp is a speech defect

explanation.surface: An elderly person's lisp comes back in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests an elderly person, but it is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet; 'returns' and 'in' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fifth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet, a character of an old script.

clue.text: …compared with such as Edward

parts.note: like means such as
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone was set beside a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to compare, so the past forms match.

clue.text: Some not unappetising food

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A litotes describing a meal as fairly tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: This oily sea fish is eaten widely, so it is a food.

clue.text: in diplomacy, one must be silent

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Diplomats must keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood without being spoken, so unspoken or silent.

clue.text: Snooper pays out in counterfeit kroner

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of order
counterfeit suggests the letters are faked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy pays with forged Scandinavian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' and 'counterfeit' both signal the shuffle of PAYS and KRONER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody who pries into others' affairs is a snooper.

clue.text: Bowl used in the house

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl a ball pitching at the batsman's feet
the royal dynasty that fought Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.walkthrough: A YORKER is a cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's feet; to bowl one is to york him.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket verb for bowling a full-pitched ball, and the English royal dynasty.

clue.text: It's a river

parts.note: It means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A plain statement that something is a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention; the whole clue defines this river of France and Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A tributary of the Moselle flowing through France and Germany.

clue.text: Turn up to help, we hear, as a favour

indicators.note: we hear says the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to cock is to turn up (a hat brim), and aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to lend a hand as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a favour' is not a kindness but a ribbon or rosette worn as a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette worn on a hat is a favour in the old sense of a ribbon badge.

clue.text: Reunite disunited train

indicators.note: disunited says the letters of the preceding word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring a separated railway train back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of attendants following a dignitary is called a train.

clue.text: In match, a series of successful strokes can decide the set

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
a break in snooker or billiards is a run of successful shots

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator notes that a run of good shots in a game can win a set.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE is a sports match (a cup tie), BREAK a snooker run; the definition is descriptive.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a deciding game played at six games all settles who wins the set.

clue.text: Jazz man engaged in commerce

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A jazz musician went into business.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD is traditional jazz, popular in 1950s-60s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bought and sold goods is to have done business, engaged in commerce.
